newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re says no change in SAFR deal.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re says no change in SAFR deal.

text.p: Swiss Reinsurance Co said it wil go through with a planned acquisition and quick resale of France's Societe Anonyme Francaise de Reassurances (SAFR) despite withdrawing a request for EU approval.
A Swiss Re spokesman said the group no longer needed European Commission approval for buying the remainder of SAFR because it would be sold right away to a non-EU compnay, Bermuda-based Partner Re.
"The transaction as announced over Easter has not changed," spokesman Andreas Jaeggi said about the plan made public on March 31.

Jaeggi said EU rules had required Swiss Re -- which already held a 21.6 percent stake in SAFR -- to report to the Commission when it announced initial plans in February to buy the remainder of the Paris-based company.
"There is no reason for a review by the European Commisiion now because SAFR will go to Partner RE, not Swiss Re," Jaeggi told Reuters.
Swiss Re said last month it would sell Paris-based SAFR to Partner Re for a capital gain of 100 million Swiss francs. Partner Re valued the deal at $950 million.
Following the complicated deal, Swiss Re would boost its stake in PartnerRe to 21.8 percent form an earlier 11.1 percent. - Zurich Newsroom +41-1-631 7340
